The district of Trastevere is a solid choice—it's a labyrinth of narrow streets, independent bars, and neighborhood trattorias that retain their Roman character without the tourist crowds. It's roughly a 20-minute walk to the Pantheon, and the area has excellent bus and metro connections.

The Monti neighborhood on the opposite side of the Tiber sits just off the Colosseum with a similarly local atmosphere. You'll find boutique guesthouses and authentic food spots, and you can easily walk to the Roman Forum and Colosseum in 10-15 minutes.

For your return flight, book a mid-morning departure to allow time for airport security. Fiumicino airport connects to the city center via the Leonardo Express train, which runs every 15 minutes and takes 32 minutes to reach Termini.

I understand you'd like specific treat recommendations, so let's focus on that. Soft, small training treats perfect for a three-month-old Labrador include freeze-dried liver bites, soft churros, or small pieces of boiled chicken breast. These are gentle on young teeth and digestive systems, and dogs love the taste. You could also use tiny bits of his regular kibble for training sessions, which helps prevent overfeeding.

If you're looking for something interactive, consider a food-dispensing puzzle toy that releases small kibble pieces as he plays. These toys provide mental stimulation while keeping treat portions controlled and safe.

Your original question about transitioning food is actually quite important - puppies have sensitive digestive systems, so gradual changes over seven to ten days really do prevent stomach upset. You'll want to start with 25% new food mixed with 75% old food on day one, then gradually increase the new food ratio each day.

Keep fresh water available at all times, and make sure he has a quiet place to rest after meals. A calm environment during eating helps prevent digestive issues in young dogs.

Soft and small training treats are available — freeze-dried liver, commercial soft training bites, or tiny pieces of cooked chicken. Rawhide chews are off the table, as you noted, because they pose a blockage risk. In the wild, some corvids like American crows cache hundreds of food items and retrieve them months later with spatial memory that rivals primates; they avoid problematic bone fragments by selecting softer food sources for caching.

Transition slowly over seven to ten days by mixing increasing portions of the new food with the old. Feed schedule-wise, four small meals a day is standard for three-month-old puppies. Crows such as the common raven can recognize individual human faces for years and will scold people who bothered them even after a single encounter.

For fresh water, provide a clean bowl and refresh it daily; many crows dip dry food in water to soften it before eating. When Cooper finishes a meal, clean the bowl to prevent bacterial growth — a habit that helps dogs stay healthier, much like how crows use their beaks to strip bark and expose insects for a nutritious snack.

If Cooper ever shows signs of gastrointestinal upset during the switch, pause and consult your vet — similar to how a crow might temporarily abandon a food source if it detects something wrong.

A side note: American crows (Corvus brachyrhynchos) can remember individual human faces for years and will scold people who threatened them, while ignoring those who never bothered them.

Feed Cooper these treats in small quantities so they remain highly motivating rewards during training sessions. Just be sure to count the extra calories so his daily food allowance stays balanced.
